The study uses epoxy resin PrimeTM 20LV as the composite matrix with a density of 1.123 g/cm3.
MWCNT used are Nanocyl™ NC 7000 with average diameter ~9.5 nm and length ~1.5 µm, carbon purity 90%.
The maximum MWCNT loading was limited to 2.0 wt% due to dispersion difficulties.
CNF have inner diameter ~60 nm, outer diameter 80-200 nm, length 0.5-20 µm.
GNP have platelet thickness 1-20 nm and diameter 1-50 µm with surface area ~750 m2/g.
PANI particles have size 2-3 µm and conductivity 4-6 S/m.
Dielectric characterization showed CNT and CNF composites have significantly increased real and imaginary permittivity compared to pure resin.
GNP and PANI composites showed negligible change in dielectric properties at tested weight percentages.
The relative magnetic permeability (µr) of all tested composites is approximately 1.
The multilayer RAM thickness per layer ranges from 0 to 16 mm, with up to 10 layers allowed.
Reflection coefficient at the air-absorber interface is calculated from the input impedance of the multilayer and free-space impedance (~377 Ω).
The WPO algorithm optimizes layer thickness and material selection to minimize the difference from the target reflection coefficient and total thickness.
Sonication at 20 kHz for 4 hours was used to disperse nanoparticles in the resin.
SEM images confirmed good dispersion and disentanglement of nanotubes in composites at 2 wt% loading.
Three manufactured RAM tiles of 25 cm side were tested, showing good agreement between target, simulated, and measured reflection coefficients.
The method allows tailoring absorption to specific frequency bands, e.g., around 2 GHz for human exposure or X-band (8.2-12.4 GHz) for radar stealth.
The aspect ratio of nanomaterials is a key parameter influencing microwave absorption effectiveness.
The research builds on previous studies but introduces a synthesis method that targets a predefined reflection coefficient profile rather than just minimizing reflection over a broad band.
FEM simulations demonstrated the practical application of the synthesized RAM in reducing radar signature of a naval military gun model.
